question: Should LINE sticker support be scoped to a bundled LINE-plugin send path with separate inbound metadata and ClawHub catalog work, or should OpenClaw add a broader channel-agnostic sticker payload/skill surface?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the original request crosses core reply payload design, bundled plugin behavior, inbound context semantics, and new skill/catalog packaging policy.

options.title: LINE send first, ClawHub catalog
options.body: Add a narrow LINE-owned channelData sticker send path, track inbound packageId/stickerId separately, and publish catalog/editor as a ClawHub skill or bundle.

options.title: Design a cross-channel sticker abstraction
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define a shared reply payload or plugin SDK contract that covers LINE, WhatsApp, Telegram, and Discord sticker semantics.

options.title: Defer core changes
options.body: Leave sticker selection/catalog work entirely to ClawHub and revisit bundled LINE send support only with stronger maintainer sponsorship and live proof.

recommendation.title: LINE send first, ClawHub catalog
recommendation.body: Add a narrow LINE-owned channelData sticker send path, track inbound packageId/stickerId separately, and publish catalog/editor as a ClawHub skill or bundle.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent plugin SDK and LINE seam history plus product-boundary involvement make this the best available routing candidate.
